exposure: maternal obesity (BMI ≥ 30 at end of pregnancy)
maternal normal weight (BMI 18.5-25 at end of pregnancy)
cohort: Patients who gave birth at Farhat Hached Sousse University Hospital and the Maternity and Neonatology Hospital of Monastir between February 1 and March 31, 2019, divided into groups based on their BMI at the end of pregnancy.
finding: Maternal obesity (BMI ≥ 30) is associated with an increased risk of maternal complications during pregnancy, labor, delivery, and postpartum, as well as various adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Obese patients experienced more labor abnormalities, with higher rates of cesarean section (17% vs. 3%) and instrumental delivery (15% vs. 7%) compared to normal weight women.
